text:
zoe: heads-up — new flaky behavior in streaming quickstart when reconciling SSE resumes. Seen in browser and Node example apps.

omar: quick summary?

zoe: repro steps in examples/streaming-resume: start stream, force a client abort while the server is writing a multi-event batch, reconnect with Last-Event-ID. Sometimes the last event reappears.

lee: do you have raw frame captures?

zoe: pasted snippet from capture: server writes:

id: 777
data: {"tok":"alpha"}

id: 778
data: {"tok":"beta"}

But the client read returned a single buffer like:

"data: {\"tok\":\"alpha\"}\ndata: {\"tok\":\"beta\"}\n"

and the connection was aborted after that read in the client. When we reconnect with Last-Event-ID: 777 the server re-emits 777 and client emits alpha again.

ciara: classic middlebox behavior — proxies/nginx can coalesce writes. TLS/HTTP2 frames don't preserve app-level boundaries.

lee: what's the Node parser doing? Waiting for the double CRLF? That could delay partial delivery and make timeouts worse.

zoe: the sample uses a simple split-on-"\r?\n\r?\n" approach. Works usually, but when events are coalesced the detection is brittle. Also the SDK doesn't dedupe by `id` across reconnects so duplicate tokens surface to user code.

omar: for parity and DX: (1) add dedupe-by-id in Node + Go SDKs (configurable, small memory bound), (2) add a lenient parser option that flushes partial events after a short configurable timeout (like 40ms) so we don't wait for a trailing blank line.

stream-bot: perf alert: quickstart-staging shows a small uptick in SSE reconnects around 2026-03-25T18:05:00Z :warning:

ciara: implementation notes: dedupe handled cheaply with a ring buffer of last N ids (default 1024) with TTL to GC; expose `id` field in emitted event for apps that want to dedupe themselves.

lee: parser idea: default is strict (no change). Add `sse.lenientFlushMs` default 0. If set >0 and we detect a single LF boundary, start a timer for that ms and emit whatever parsed when timer fires unless more bytes arrive. This reduces latency in coalesced scenarios.

omar: add integration tests using docker-compose with nginx/haproxy configured to coalesce and split writes. Tests should simulate abort mid-batch, reconnect with Last-Event-ID, and assert no duplicate tokens delivered when dedupe is enabled.

zoe: short-term workarounds for users: server-side immediate flush on SSE endpoints, or include an incrementing `seq` inside the JSON and dedupe at the application level. We'll add a quick note in onboarding docs.

ciara: also add an observability metric `sse.dedup.skipped` and a debug trace when SDK drops a duplicate to help ops triage.

stream-bot: action items created: SDKS-1823 (Node dedupe + lenient parse), SDKS-1824 (Go parity), INTEG-77 (nginx/haproxy harness).

omar: I'll open the GH issue with suggested unit tests and a small E2E that asserts dedupe correctness.

zoe: I'll add a reproducible nginx config + curl script in examples/streaming-resume so reviewers can run locally. Will link the PR when ready. :thumbsup:

lee: once PRs land let's enforce an E2E in SDK CI that simulates abort+resume to prevent regressions. That should reduce onboarding flakes.

ciara: note for docs: explain tradeoffs between strict SSE semantics and lenient behavior; default to strict but surface the lenient option in quickstart to reduce friction for new users.

zoe: filing refs: https://git.internal/repo/issue/1823 and PR https://git.internal/repo/pulls/9001 — comments welcome.
